events.title: Microsoft and the US government propose a settlement
events.description: The agreement would restrict some business practices. Court review and other legal steps remain.

events.title: Euro cash enters everyday use
events.description: Twelve countries introduce euro notes and coins.

events.title: Columbia is lost
events.description: The space shuttle breaks apart during its return to Earth, killing its seven crew members.

events.title: Hurricane Katrina strikes
events.description: The hurricane devastates Gulf Coast communities and creates an enormous need for rescue and recovery.

what_happened_next.text:
Microsoft finished about 38% above its start, PepsiCo about 28% above, and Coca-Cola about 26% below. The international share basket came close to Microsoft, while the U.S. basket ended slightly behind cash. Two companies selling familiar foods and drinks did not give investors the same result.

PepsiCo completed its Quaker Oats merger in 2001, adding brands such as Quaker and Gatorade. Coca-Cola launched C2 in 2004, but later reported that its North American results fell short of expectations. Microsoft announced a one-time $3-per-share dividend in 2004, scheduled for December, along with plans to buy back shares. These company events explain what changed in their businesses or cash plans, not exactly why each share moved.

Euro cash entered everyday use in 2002. The Columbia shuttle was lost in 2003, and Hurricane Katrina devastated Gulf Coast communities in 2005. Science, business and disasters all formed part of these years, with very different effects on people. Buying a product often is different from knowing what its company’s stock will be worth later; compare the result with the reasons you chose at the start.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The presidential election was finally settled. Drink makers chased new markets, and scientists studied signs of ancient water on Mars.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Similar brands could take different paths. The international share basket added businesses outside the US, with different opportunities, risks and currencies.
reflection.what_faded_away: A new drink deal or a year-end economic prediction could not settle the five-year ranking. The story continued long after the headlines changed.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: Nobody knew the exact company outcomes or the shocks ahead. A familiar household product was not a guarantee against losing money.

hot:2000-12:pepsico.text: PepsiCo completed its merger with Quaker Oats on August 2, 2001, combining businesses with about $25 billion in annual sales. The deal brought Quaker and Gatorade into PepsiCo’s mix of drinks and snacks, giving it more products to sell in stores and sports venues.

hot:2000-12:coca-cola.text: Coca-Cola introduced C2 in North America in June 2004, hoping shoppers would like a cola with less sugar and fewer calories. Sales fell short of the company’s hopes. Its North American retail business also sold 1% less drink volume that year, showing the difficulty of growing in that market.

hot:2000-12:microsoft.text: In July 2004, Microsoft announced a one-time $3-per-share dividend to be paid in December, alongside regular dividends and stock buybacks. The payout returned company cash to shareholders, giving them a special payment in addition to the regular dividend.
